es.summary: Inflamación del hígado causada por consumo excesivo y prolongado de alcohol. Puede presentarse de forma aguda o progresar a crónica y cirrosis.
key_points: Inflamación hepática por toxicidad del alcohol
Ictericia, dolor epigástrico, náuseas y anorexia son comunes
Puede evolucionar a cirrosis e insuficiencia hepática

pathophysiology: El alcohol se metaboliza a acetaldehído, tóxico para hepatocitos
Daño oxidativo genera necrosis y apoptosis hepática
Respuesta inflamatoria produce infiltrado de neutrófilos y macrófagos
Fibrosis progresiva por activación de células de Kupffer y fibroblastos
risk_factors: Consumo >60 g/día en hombres o >40 g/día en mujeres durante años
Genética que afecta la actividad de ADH/ALDH
signs_symptoms: Dolor o molestia en hipocondrio derecho
Ascitis y edema en etapas avanzadas
diagnostics: AST y ALT elevados; AST/ALT >2 (ej. AST ≈ 300 U/L, ALT ≈ 120 U/L)
treatment: Reposo y nutrición hipercalórica con suplementos de tiamina
Hidratación IV con solución salina isotónica
nursing_care: Monitorear signos vitales y nivel de conciencia cada 4 h
Evaluar dolor epigástrico y respuesta a analgésicos
Observar cambios en color de piel y mucosas
Mantener reposo en posición semisentado para facilitar respiración
patient_teaching: Importancia de la abstinencia total de alcohol y recursos de apoyo
Dieta alta en proteínas y calorías, evitar ayuno prolongado
Tomar suplementos de tiamina antes de iniciar hidratación IV
Reconocer signos de sangrado gastrointestinal y buscar ayuda inmediata

interventions.action: Monitorear electrolitos séricos cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detectar alteraciones tempranas y guiar terapia de reposición

interventions.action: Evaluar ingesta y pérdida de líquidos (I/O) cada turno
interventions.rationale: Identificar desequilibrios de volumen que afectan electrolitos

interventions.action: Administrar solución salina isotónica IV según prescripción
Ofrecer alimentos ricos en potasio (plátano, papaya) y bajo en sodio
interventions.rationale: Contribuir al mantenimiento de niveles electrolíticos

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre evitar diuréticos sin indicación
interventions.rationale: Prevenir pérdida excesiva de sodio y potasio

interventions.action: Registrar y reportar cualquier arritmia o alteración del ECG
interventions.rationale: Las alteraciones electrolíticas pueden desencadenar eventos cardíacos

evidenced_by: Cansancio al realizar actividades de la vida diaria
Disminución de la tolerancia al ejercicio leve
Dolor abdominal que empeora con el esfuerzo
outcomes: Capacidad para realizar ADL con mínima fatiga (escala 0‑10 ≤3)
Nivel de energía mejorado en 48 h (escala 0‑10 ≥6)

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y tolerancia al esfuerzo cada turno
interventions.rationale: Establecer línea base y detectar deterioro

interventions.action: Planificar actividades en bloques de 10‑15 min con descansos
Fomentar posición semisentada durante actividades que requieran esfuerzo
Monitorear signos vitales antes y después de la actividad
Enseñar técnicas de conservación de energía (uso de ayudas, delegar tareas)
interventions.rationale: Optimizar desempeño funcional sin exacerbar síntomas

interventions.action: Coordinar con fisioterapia para programa de ejercicio gradual

en.summary: Inflammation of the liver caused by excessive and prolonged alcohol consumption. It can present acutely or progress to chronic disease and cirrhosis.
key_points: Hepatic inflammation due to alcohol toxicity
AST is usually >ALT with a ratio >2
Jaundice, epigastric pain, nausea, and anorexia are common
May progress to cirrhosis and hepatic failure

pathophysiology: Alcohol is metabolized to acetaldehyde, toxic to hepatocytes
Oxidative damage causes hepatic necrosis and apoptosis
Inflammatory response produces neutrophil and macrophage infiltrate
Progressive fibrosis from Kupffer cell and fibroblast activation
risk_factors: Consumption >60 g/day in men or >40 g/day in women for years
signs_symptoms: Ascites and edema in advanced stages
diagnostics: Elevated AST and ALT; AST/ALT >2 (e.g., AST ≈ 300 U/L, ALT ≈ 120 U/L)
treatment: Rest and hypercaloric nutrition with thiamine supplements
nursing_care: Monitor vital signs and level of consciousness every 4 h
Assess epigastric pain and analgesic response
Observe changes in skin and mucous color
Maintain semi‑recumbent rest to aid breathing
patient_teaching: Importance of total alcohol abstinence and support resources
High‑protein, high‑calorie diet, avoid prolonged fasting
Take thiamine supplements before starting IV hydration
Recognize GI bleeding signs and seek immediate help

interventions.action: Monitor serum electrolytes every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detect early changes and guide replacement therapy

interventions.action: Assess fluid intake and output each shift
Administer isotonic saline IV per prescription
Offer potassium‑rich foods (banana, papaya) and low‑sodium options
Educate patient on avoiding unnecessary diuretics
interventions.rationale: Prevent excessive sodium and potassium loss

interventions.action: Record and report any arrhythmia or ECG changes
interventions.rationale: Electrolyte disturbances can trigger cardiac events

outcomes: Ability to perform ADLs with minimal fatigue (scale 0‑10 ≤3)

interventions.action: Assess energy level and exertion tolerance each shift
Plan activities in 10‑15 min blocks with rest
Encourage semi‑recumbent position during effortful activities
Monitor vital signs before and after activity
Teach energy conservation techniques (use aids, delegate tasks)
Coordinate with PT for gradual exercise program

summary.0.quote: Alcoholic hepatitis is caused by heavy alcohol use

summary.1.quote: The infection can become chronic and may progress to cirrhosis or liver failure; it is also associated with liver cancer.

key_points.2.quote: If you do have symptoms, they may include: Fever Fatigue Loss of appetite Nausea and/or vomiting Abdominal pain Dark urine Clay-colored bowel movements Joint pain Jaundice , yellowing of your skin and eyes

key_points.3.quote: The infection can become chronic and may progress to cirrhosis or liver failure; it is also associated with liver cancer.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Late-stage findings include confusion, coma, ascites, and GI bleeding

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: When the liver is not functioning normally, the blood will contain elevated levels of alkaline phosphatase, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, direct bilirubin, total bilirubin, serum albumin, serum total protein, and calculated globulin; the albumin to globulin (A/G) ratio will also be elevated.

sections.treatment.4.quote: If your chronic hepatitis leads to liver failure or liver cancer, you may need a liver transplant .

sections.complications.0.quote: Chronic hepatitis can lead to complications such as cirrhosis (scarring of the liver), liver failure, and liver cancer .
